rules.why: A handful of lines across a few files has no architecture to reason about - the whole diff fits in one read, and depth buys nothing but spend. The cheaper class on both sides finds the same typo, and quota exhaustion is the real failure mode of this flow, not a missed nit.
The ordinary PR. Both finders think as hard as each other, which is the condition review-finder-pi.sh states for a bid being worth merging at all.

Past ~800 changed lines the cross-file reasoning is the review, and a missed blocker costs more than the spend. The rung timeout rises with the effort deliberately: xhigh inside a 600s deadline buys reasoning the deadline then kills, sealing nothing.
